intent: My sister keeps gifting me teas and coffees plastered with claims: detox blends, antioxidant-packed matcha, mushroom coffee promising crash-free focus, low-acid roasts that are supposedly gentle on the stomach. I drink this stuff every day and I'm tired of not knowing what's real. Before I restock my cupboard I want to figure out which of these claims actually hold up scientifically and which are pure label decoration, and whether the people who bought these products noticed anything at all. If some claims are legit, point me at the honest versions worth paying for and tell me what to skip.

intent_v1_legacy: With all the arguing about vaccines lately I realized I don't actually know how they were invented or how the methods evolved. Can you take me through the history, from the very first crude vaccines, through Pasteur's breakthroughs, the big 20th-century leaps like the polio vaccine, all the way to today's DNA and mRNA ones? I'd like to follow it as a story and understand what each generation did differently. A clear rundown of the main vaccine types we use now would help, and any old myths people have finally stopped believing.
